## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a CRITICAL pump problem that requires immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating and prevents normal system operation. All other components are in good condition, but this deficiency must be resolved before the system can function reliably.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined scum and sludge depth is 11 inches, representing 22.9% of the total fluid depth. This is within the normal operating range and does not require pumping at this time.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank | Good | Concrete construction, 1,250-gallon capacity |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Light soiling; cleaned and reseated during this visit |
| Effluent Pump | CRITICAL | See Pump Amp Draw section below |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals observed |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no ponding or breakout observed |

## PUMP AMP DRAW
**Measured Current:** 1.6A  
**Nameplate Rating:** 7.2A  
**Load Percentage:** 22.2% FLA  
**Status:** CRITICAL - No Load

The pump motor is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load -- the impeller is not moving fluid against system pressure. The most likely causes are:
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-run condition (no fluid reaching the pump inlet)

A pump running without load generates heat that the fluid normally dissipates. Continued operation under this condition risks motor burnout and failure.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. A qualified technician must inspect the pump discharge line for disconnection or blockage, verify impeller integrity, and confirm that fluid is reaching the pump inlet. Do not operate the system until the pump load problem is resolved.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is repaired and verified operational.
- The effluent filter soiling is light and the filter was cleaned during this visit. Monitor at the next maintenance visit.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition because the motor is working without the cooling effect of fluid flow, which can cause it to overheat and fail. The problem could be a broken internal part, a disconnected pipe, or a blockage preventing water from reaching the pump. A service technician needs to diagnose and repair this before your system can treat wastewater properly.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at a healthy level (about 23% of tank volume). You do not need pumping at this time. Keep the system healthy by avoiding non-biodegradable items -- wipes, paper towels, grease, and harsh chemicals all slow treatment and accelerate solids buildup.
